conversations.question: Why was decision d_002_safety_veto blocked by safety?
conversations.answer: Decision d_002_safety_veto for user user_delhi_2310 evaluated a delayed charging plan (start 22:30). Perception estimated an arrival SOC lower bound (q10) of 0.82, which breached the mandatory reserve threshold of 0.90 (90% confidence invariant). In accordance with AGENTS.md Rule 1.2, Safety Filter #1 executed a hard veto before the contextual bandit could evaluate the plan, preserving driver range and sending no nudge.

conversations.question: Why did you nudge fewer people at 19:30 (d_003_learned_silence)?
conversations.answer: At 19:30, user user_delhi_0044 already routine-charges during the overnight off-peak window. LinTS evaluated an estimated uplift of -0.03 kWh (non-positive), meaning the user would shift charging anyway without persuasion. GridNudge selected the 'none' first-class action to preserve driver attention budget and avoid alert fatigue.

conversations.question: How does GridNudge compare against Broadcast under the heatwave?
conversations.answer: Under the 5-seed heatwave benchmark with common random numbers, GridNudge achieved evening peak reduction to 20.47 MW with 0 attributable stranded trips and 0.53 nudges/user/day (vs 0.99 for Broadcast B1), preserving driver attention and avoiding rebound peaks.
